key_insight: Reward models inherit systematic value and preference biases from their LLM pretraining priors, producing consistent differences in moral, social, and political judgments across models even after fine-tuning for reward tasks.
problem_solved: Identifies and quantifies how pretraining representations shape reward-model outputs, revealing a previously underexplored source of bias in alignment pipelines (RMs initialized from pretrained LLMs).
method: Survey of 10 leading open‑weight reward models initialized from different pretrained LLMs and fine‑tuning procedures.

Evaluation using validated psycholinguistic corpora spanning moral, social, and political value dimensions; statistical comparison of RM responses across dimensions and against pretrained LLM baselines.
Controlled analyses isolating effects of initialization vs. post‑training (e.g., comparing models with different pretraining priors and fine‑tuning histories).
impact: Practitioners should treat reward-model choice and pretraining history as a critical alignment vector—biases in pretrained LLMs can propagate into RMs and affect downstream RLHF outcomes, evaluation, and deployment safety decisions.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Pretrained LLM → RM initialization → fine‑tuning/RLHF → observed biased outputs (annotated arrows showing inheritance).
Bar/line chart: Comparison of bias scores across the 10 RMs for several value dimensions (moral, political, social).
Heatmap: Per‑model vs. per‑dimension intensity of value biases to highlight patterns and clusters.
Icon set: model/brain, scale (ethics), dataset/magnifier, and deployment/server to convey pipeline and consequences.
paper_title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
paper_authors: Brian Christian, Jessica A. F. Thompson, Elle Michelle Yang, Vincent Adam, Hannah Rose Kirk
